abstract: Prelimbic cortex activity is known to promote fear expression, yet its specific representational function within the fear circuit remains unclear. We recorded prelimbic single-unit activity in rats undergoing probabilistic fear discrimination and identified three complementary levels of representation. Prelimbic neurons represented diverse danger-modulated behaviors, not just freezing, such that the initiation and cessation of five behaviors could be accurately decoded from ensemble firing. Behavioral representations were embedded within a veridical representation of the environmental threat structure, in which the majority of prelimbic neurons tuned cue firing to learned threat probability-regardless of behavior coding. This threat probability representation supported precise decoding of learned cue identity and partial decoding of threat cue timing, both of which were degraded when discriminative responding was poor. Prelimbic outcome firing was dominated by inhibition to predicted shock. Together, these results reveal that prelimbic cortex firing is organized around threat at multiple levels, from rich representations of danger-modulated behavior to veridical probabilistic threat predictions and predictive outcome signals.
